title: Design adapter monitoring/alerting strategy
description:
## Question

How does the system detect and alert on an Adapter breaking (HTML selector changed, internal JSON API shape changed, or anti-bot blocking kicked in), given confirmed decisions: alerts reuse the Telegram bot channel, and alerting fires after consecutive failures rather than on the first failure?

This ticket is blocked on the platform-API prototype ticket: the real failure modes (structured JSON error vs. HTML parse exception vs. CAPTCHA/block page vs. timeout) determine what "failure" even means to detect, which can't be designed from guesswork. Once unblocked, grill: what counts as a distinguishable failure per platform, the consecutive-failure threshold, what the Telegram alert message contains, whether a broken Adapter auto-pauses (stops attempting further runs until acknowledged) or keeps retrying on schedule, and how this is surfaced on the dashboard (not just Telegram).

title: Design CV/cover-letter HTML template
description:
## Question

What does the single generic Blade HTML template (rendered to PDF via Browsershot) for a TailoredApplication's CV and cover letter look like — layout, sections, and how it binds to TailoredApplication's structured JSON fields?

This ticket is blocked on both the MasterProfile schema ticket and the canonical Job model ticket: the template can't be designed until the fields it renders (experience entries, skills, education, projects from MasterProfile; job title/company/description context from Job) are locked. Per the map's Destination, this is ONE generic template for v1 — no per-role variants (SA vs QA out of scope). Grill: CV layout/sections, cover-letter structure, how the "reframed description/achievement" text from TailoredApplication slots in without touching the locked facts (title/company/period), and whether CV and cover letter are one PDF or two separate PDFs.
design:
## CV/cover-letter template design (v1)

### Output

Two separate PDFs per TailoredApplication — `cv.pdf` and `cover_letter.pdf` — each its own
Blade view, each its own Browsershot render call. Not a combined single-PDF document.

### Visual style

Minimalist, single-column, pure black text (no accent colors). Thin horizontal rule under
each section heading to separate sections. Font: Inter, self-hosted (Regular + Bold/Semibold
`.woff2` bundled with the template assets, `@font-face`'d in) — no Google Fonts CDN dependency,
so PDF rendering in the queue worker never depends on outbound network access at render time.
Natural page-length flow, no hard single-page cap (Browsershot/PDF paginate natively).

### CV sections (in order; a section is omitted entirely — no heading rendered — if its
underlying data is empty)

1. **Header** — name, email, phone, location, links (all facts). Optional profile photo:
   fixed 100x100px, rounded-square (not circular), positioned top-left beside the text block,
   shown only if `show_photo` is true. No role tagline under the name (MasterProfile has no
   "current title" concept; deriving one from the latest Experience entry was rejected as an
   undesired implicit fact-derivation rule).
2. **Professional Summary** — reframed text, single field (not array/ID-keyed — it's a
   MasterProfile singleton).
3. **Skills** — grouped by category, one line per category (e.g. "Programming Languages:
   JavaScript, Python, Go"). Copied verbatim from MasterProfile; skills never go through the
   Gemini call at all, since they're pure facts with nothing to reframe.
4. **Experience** — reverse-chronological. Per entry: facts (title, company, location,
   start/end date, employment_type) rendered as-is; description reframed; achievements
   reframed as a bulleted list that may shrink (AI can drop irrelevant bullets for a sharper
   CV) but never grow beyond MasterProfile's original count (inventing achievements would
   violate the "reframe only" rule).
5. **Education** — same fact/reframe split as Experience.
6. **Projects** — same fact/reframe split as Experience.

Date display format: `"Jan 2022 – Mar 2024"` (month abbreviation + 4-digit year, en dash),
`"Present"` when `is_current` is true.

### Cover letter structure

Letterhead (name/contact block, no photo) → date line → subject line
`"Re: Application for {job.title}"` → greeting `"Dear {company_name} Hiring Team"` (no
recruiter-name field exists anywhere in the data model, so this is the fixed default, not
AI-generated) → `opening_paragraph` → `body_paragraphs[]` → `closing_paragraph` → sign-off
`"Sincerely, {full_name}"`. No recipient address block (no address data exists for either
Job or a hiring contact). Only the three paragraph fields are AI-generated; greeting, date,
subject, and sign-off are deterministic, app-assembled from Job/MasterProfile facts.

### TailoredApplication JSON binding (self-contained snapshots — template renders entirely
from this JSON, no MasterProfile re-join at render time; this is the audit-trail mechanism
n58.3 already committed to)

**`cv_data`**:
- `personal_info`: full_name, email, phone, location, links, professional_summary
  (reframed), photo_path, show_photo — all copied/reframed at generation time
- `skills`: copied verbatim from MasterProfile (category groupings intact)
- `experience[]` / `education[]` / `projects[]`: each entry object keyed by its
  MasterProfile row's `entry_id`, carrying the copied facts (title/company/dates/etc.)
  plus the reframed description/achievements

**`cover_letter_data`**:
- Assembled facts: greeting, date, subject, sign_off
- AI-generated: opening_paragraph, body_paragraphs[], closing_paragraph

### Gemini `responseSchema` scope

Deliberately narrower than the full snapshot above — only what the AI actually writes:
- Per Experience/Education/Project entry: `{entry_id, description, achievements[]}`
- Cover letter: `{opening_paragraph, body_paragraphs[], closing_paragraph}`

The request includes each MasterProfile entry's `entry_id` so the response is ID-keyed
rather than positionally matched — robust to the AI skipping/reordering entries, and makes
programmatic fact-validation (the map's fixed pre-render check) a direct lookup: fetch the
MasterProfile row by `entry_id`, confirm the AI didn't touch title/company/period, since the
AI response never even carries those fields.

### MasterProfile schema amendment (reopens n58.3's closed design)

Adds two fields to MasterProfile (personal info) to support the optional photo:
- `photo_path` — nullable, dashboard-uploaded file
- `show_photo` — boolean, independent of whether a photo is uploaded, so uploading a photo
  doesn't force it onto every CV

## Decisions

- Two PDFs, not one — matches how job platforms/company portals request uploads separately
  (CV required, cover letter often distinct/optional), and keeps each layout independent.
- ATS-friendly minimalist style chosen deliberately over a more visually distinctive
  multi-column/sidebar layout, since documents flow through automated parsers on
  Glints/JobStreet and third-party ATS after that.
- Skills bypass the AI entirely (never sent to or received from Gemini) — they're pure facts
  per n58.3's fact/reframe split, so round-tripping them through the model would only add
  token cost and a risk surface for unwanted edits, with no upside.
- Achievements may shrink but never grow when reframed — a deliberate reading of "reframe
  only" (n58's fixed constraint): curating down to the most relevant bullets is reframing;
  fabricating new ones is not.
- Cover letter's greeting/date/subject/sign-off are template-assembled facts, not AI output —
  only the narrative paragraphs are actually generated, keeping the Gemini responseSchema
  minimal and validation trivial (nothing fact-bearing for the AI to get wrong there).
- TailoredApplication JSON is a full self-contained snapshot (facts + reframed content),
  keyed by MasterProfile entry_id, for both cv_data and cover_letter_data — consistent with
  n58.3's stated audit-trail rationale, and means template rendering never needs to re-join
  live MasterProfile state (which could have changed since generation).
- Font is Inter, self-hosted rather than CDN-loaded — Browsershot renders in a queue worker
  context where an outbound font fetch at render time is an unnecessary failure mode.
- Photo is optional via a dedicated `show_photo` toggle separate from `photo_path` — amends
  n58.3's MasterProfile schema (photo wasn't in scope there). Positioned top-left,
  100x100px rounded-square, only in the CV header (never on the cover letter letterhead).

Grilled and confirmed with user: 4 rounds, 18 questions.
close_reason: CV/cover-letter template grilled and confirmed with user (4 rounds, 18 questions). Two separate PDFs (cv.pdf/cover_letter.pdf), minimalist single-column Inter-font layout with section-separator rules, CV section list/order with omit-if-empty, ID-keyed fact+reframe JSON snapshot binding for TailoredApplication (cv_data/cover_letter_data), narrow Gemini responseSchema (skills bypass AI entirely; cover letter greeting/date/subject/sign-off are app-assembled facts, not AI output), achievements may shrink but not grow when reframed, optional photo toggle (amends MasterProfile from n58.3). Full design recorded in issue design field.

title: Design canonical Job model
description:
## Question

What is the canonical shape of a Job — the normalized model every Adapter (Glints, JobStreet) produces regardless of source? Which fields are "core" (present and harmonized across both platforms) vs "extra" (platform-specific, stored loosely)?

This ticket is blocked on the platform-API prototype ticket: the real field availability (e.g. salary range, remote/onsite tags, seniority level) from Glints and JobStreet needs to be known before the canonical model is locked, otherwise the schema is guesswork. Once unblocked, grill: field list and types, how platform+external_id (the dedup key) is stored, how posted_date is normalized across platforms with different date formats/granularity, and how a Job links to the SearchProfile match(es) that surfaced it.
design:
## Canonical Job model (v1)

### Job (core columns)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| platform | enum: glints \| jobstreet | Part of the dedup key |
| external_id | string | Platform's raw job id; part of the dedup key |
| title | string | |
| company_name | string | No separate normalized Company entity in v1 |
| location | string (free text) | Same shape as SearchProfile.location |
| country_code | string | For JobStreet, populated from the Adapter/search request context (id.jobstreet.com is ID-scoped), not parsed from the job payload |
| url | string | The one link the dashboard sends the user to in order to apply/view — Glints' externalApplyURL, JobStreet's url; no separate detail-page field |
| description | text | Glints descriptionJsonString, JobStreet abstract — richness differs by platform, still one field |
| work_arrangement | enum: remote \| onsite \| hybrid \| unspecified | "unspecified" (not "any" — that's a SearchProfile filter wildcard, not a Job attribute) |
| job_type | enum: full_time \| part_time \| contract \| internship \| unspecified | Same enum family as SearchProfile.job_type minus "any" |
| min_years_experience | integer, nullable | Kept as core (nullable) even though JobStreet doesn't expose it, for dashboard-consistency with the SearchProfile filter |
| max_years_experience | integer, nullable | Same rationale |
| status | enum: open \| closed \| expired \| unknown | Glints: mapped directly from its status field. JobStreet: derived from expiry if available, else `unknown` — never guessed as `open`. Re-derived on every re-poll, not fixed at first ingest |
| salary_min | numeric, nullable | |
| salary_max | numeric, nullable | |
| salary_currency | string, nullable | ISO code |
| salary_period | enum: monthly \| yearly \| unspecified, nullable | Stored as each platform reports it — no monthly↔yearly normalization (lossy); pre-formatted display strings live in raw_payload instead |
| posted_date | timestamp | Glints -> createdAt (not startDate, which is likely employment start date, or expiryDate, which is application deadline). JobStreet -> listedAt. Always the best-available real timestamp; no bucket is stored on Job (buckets are a SearchProfile query-side concept only) |
| raw_payload | JSON | Full raw platform response, not a curated subset — cheaper to mine a new field later than to re-fetch |

### Dedup key

Composite unique index `(platform, external_id)`. No synthetic combined key column — the composite index is the dedup check, run before a Job enters AI tailoring (per the map's fixed architectural decision).

### Update semantics

Upsert on dedup match: re-fetching an already-seen `(platform, external_id)` refreshes core fields and `raw_payload` from the latest response (this is what makes `status` transitions like open->closed/expired observable over time). Fields already consumed by an Application/TailoredApplication are never retroactively overwritten by a later Job refresh.

### Job <-> SearchProfile linkage

Many-to-many pivot table `job_search_profile_matches` (`job_id`, `search_profile_id`, `matched_at`), one row per first-observed (Job, SearchProfile) pair. Purely informational for v1 (dashboard "why did this appear" display) — a second SearchProfile later matching an already-deduped Job adds a pivot row but does not re-trigger notification/tailoring, since exactly one Application exists per Job regardless of match count.

### Extra/platform-specific data

Not promoted to columns for v1: Glints skills/benefits/educationLevel/gender/labels, JobStreet categories/activity-analytics-counts/seoHierarchy, and both platforms' pre-formatted salary display strings. All available via `raw_payload` if/when actually needed.

## Decisions

- Core vs extra split: a field is core only if every Adapter can populate it the same way; min/max_years_experience is a deliberate exception (kept core+nullable for dashboard consistency with the SearchProfile filter it mirrors) despite JobStreet lacking it.
- skills (Glints) and tags (JobStreet) are NOT unified into one core field — different semantics (skill list vs generic tags) — both stay in raw_payload.
- No separate Company entity; company is a plain string column on Job for v1.
- Reference facts pulled from applyr-n58.1 findings (Glints searchJobsV3 Job fields; JobStreet jobSearchV7 Job fields) as the union basis for this schema.
close_reason: Canonical Job model grilled and confirmed with user (10 questions, 2 rounds). Core/extra field split, platform+external_id dedup key (composite unique index), posted_date normalized to a real timestamp per platform (no bucket stored), status enum re-derived on upsert, structured salary columns, and a Job-SearchProfile pivot table all recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md Job definition sharpened to match (composite dedup key, core-vs-raw_payload split, upsert-not-immutable, pivot linkage).

title: Design Application status-tracking flow
description:
## Question

What states does an Application move through on the dashboard, and what are the valid transitions between them? Per CONTEXT.md, an Application exists once a Job clears dedup+match against a SearchProfile, starts before tailoring (TailoredApplication content is filled in once AI tailoring succeeds), and is reviewed/edited by the user before applying.

Grill: the full state list (e.g. pending_tailoring, needs_review, ready, applied, rejected, and whether states like "tailoring_failed" need to exist if regeneration exhausts retries), which transitions are user-triggered (dashboard actions) vs system-triggered (pipeline events), whether a user can manually edit tailored content and what that does to status, and whether closed/terminal states (applied, rejected, withdrawn) are ever reopened.
design:
## Application status-tracking flow (v1)

### States (single `status` enum column on Application)

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending_tailoring` | Created on Job dedup+match; also reused as the "regenerating" state (may still reference a prior valid TailoredApplication as fallback while a new attempt runs) |
| `tailoring_failed` | Regeneration retries exhausted; visible on dashboard with a manual retry action |
| `needs_review` | Current TailoredApplication is fact-valid; user can edit, regenerate, apply, or reject from here |
| `applied` | User manually marked it after submitting the application themselves on the platform (no auto-submit, no platform status polling) |
| `rejected` | User decided not to pursue this Job (covers both a pre-tailoring drop and a post-review drop; no separate `withdrawn` state) |

### Schema additions on Application

- `status` (enum, the 5 values above)
- `current_tailored_application_id` (nullable FK; retained across a regenerate until the new attempt replaces it, not cleared immediately)
- `applied_at` (nullable timestamp)
- `rejected_at` (nullable timestamp)
- `previous_status` (set only at the moment of a terminal transition into `applied`/`rejected`; powers Undo — no full status-history table)
- `edited_by_user` (nullable boolean, optional; editing tailored content does not itself change `status`)

### Transitions

| From | To | Trigger | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| (create) | `pending_tailoring` | system: Job clears dedup+match | |
| `pending_tailoring` | `needs_review` | system: tailoring succeeds fact validation | sends Telegram notification (the "come review this" moment) |
| `pending_tailoring` | `tailoring_failed` | system: regeneration retries exhausted | no per-Application Telegram ping — folds into n58.7's consecutive-failure alerting, not a separate channel |
| `pending_tailoring` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = pending_tailoring` |
| `tailoring_failed` | `pending_tailoring` | user: retry | |
| `tailoring_failed` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = tailoring_failed` |
| `needs_review` | `pending_tailoring` | user: regenerate | old TailoredApplication stays referenced/visible ("regenerating…") until replaced |
| `needs_review` | `applied` | user: mark applied | sets `applied_at` |
| `needs_review` | `rejected` | user: reject | `previous_status = needs_review`, sets `rejected_at` |
| `applied` | `needs_review` | user: undo | clears `applied_at` |
| `rejected` | `previous_status` | user: undo | clears `rejected_at`; restores exact prior status, not a fixed one |

### Non-status actions

- Editing tailored CV/cover-letter content in place: available while `needs_review`, does not change `status`.
- No reject-reason/notes field for v1 (no stated use case; easy to add later as a nullable column).

### UI shape

Named per-status action buttons (Reject / Retry / Regenerate / Mark Applied / Undo) driven off current `status` — not a free "change status to anything" dropdown. Avoids reachable-but-nonsensical states (e.g. jumping `pending_tailoring` straight to `applied` with no TailoredApplication to show).

### Out of scope for v1

- Tracking downstream real-world outcomes (employer-rejected, interview, offer) — would require authenticated platform integration, a different risk class than the read-only search APIs validated in n58.1.
- Status-change history log — per-state timestamps are enough; no stated need to reconstruct the full transition sequence.

Grilled and confirmed with user: 4 rounds, 15 questions total.
notes: Grilling round 1 in progress (8 questions on status modeling, pending-stage rejection, review/ready collapse, rejected/withdrawn semantics, applied semantics, tailoring-failure visibility, edit effect on status, terminal-state reopening).
close_reason: Application status flow grilled and confirmed with user (4 rounds, 15 questions). Full state list, transition table, schema fields, and undo/notification semantics recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md Application definition sharpened to match (single status enum, no separate ready state, rejected covers withdrawn, terminal undo).

title: Design MasterProfile schema and dashboard form
description:
## Question

What fields make up MasterProfile (the user's ground-truth work history, skills, education, projects — the source of truth TailoredApplication facts must match exactly), and how is it authored/edited via a dashboard form (confirmed: form-based, not a config file)?

Grill: structure of an experience entry (title, company, period, description/achievements — the fields TailoredApplication may not alter vs. may reframe), how skills and projects are represented (free text vs. structured/taggable), education entries, and what the dashboard form needs to support editing all of this (single-user, no-auth). Also confirm: is MasterProfile a single record, or versioned/snapshotted so a past TailoredApplication can be traced to the profile state it was generated from?
design:
## MasterProfile schema (v1)

Storage: single mutable `master_profiles` row (singleton, no user_id, not versioned) + relational
child tables (hasMany from MasterProfile): `experiences`, `educations`, `projects`. `skills` is a
JSON column on MasterProfile itself.

### MasterProfile (personal info)

 Field                 | Type                              | Notes
------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------------
 full_name             | string, required                  | fact
 email                 | string, required                  | fact
 phone                 | string, nullable                  | fact
 location              | string, nullable                  | fact
 professional_summary  | text, nullable                    | reframeable
 links                 | JSON {label, url}[]                | free-form, not fixed columns
 skills                | JSON {category: string, skills: string[]}[] | free-form user-defined categories

### Experience (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc)

title, company, location? (facts) | start_date, end_date?, is_current bool (facts, month+year
precision) | employment_type? enum (fact) | description text (reframeable) | achievements
string[] (reframeable) | skills_used? tags (fact, references skills)

### Education (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc)

institution, degree, field_of_study (facts) | start_date, end_date?, is_current bool (facts) |
description? text (reframeable - GPA/honors/coursework go here freeform, no dedicated fields)

### Project (hasMany, sorted by start_date desc, standalone - not linked to Experience)

name, start_date?, end_date?, is_current bool, tech_stack tags, link? url (facts) | description
text (reframeable) | achievements? string[] (reframeable)

## Decisions

- Single mutable record, no versioning/snapshotting. TailoredApplication's own copy of the facts
  it used (title/company/period etc, already required to match exactly) is sufficient audit
  trail; a full version-history table was rejected as unneeded complexity for a single-user tool
  edited infrequently.
- Fact/reframe split (locked architecturally for Experience) applies uniformly across Experience,
  Education, and Project: identifying/structural fields are immutable facts, only free-text
  `description`/`achievements` fields are AI-reframeable.
- MasterProfile's scope is sharpened beyond CONTEXT.md's original "work history, skills,
  education, and projects" to also include personal/contact info (name, email, phone, location,
  links, professional summary) - needed as the CV header's source of truth and naturally belongs
  with the rest of the ground-truth data.
- Links are a free-form {label, url}[] list, not fixed columns (linkedin_url etc) - avoids a
  migration every time a new link type appears.
- Skills are a categorized tag list (JSON column on MasterProfile, not a child table) - no
  per-skill fact/reframe distinction to track, so no need for row-level addressability.
- Experience/Education/Project are separate relational child tables (not JSON blobs on
  MasterProfile) - idiomatic Laravel, each entry independently addressable, maps directly to
  per-row CRUD on the dashboard form.
- No manual ordering - lists are always sorted by start_date descending (reverse-chronological,
  standard CV convention). No display_order field, no reorder UI.
- No per-entry inclusion/visibility toggle for v1 - every MasterProfile entry always feeds every
  TailoredApplication generation. Deferred as a `hidden` boolean addable later if it turns out to
  be needed; no stated use case yet.
- Dates are month+year precision only (day defaults to 1st internally, never shown/collected).
- `is_current` is an explicit boolean per Experience/Education entry (not inferred from null
  end_date), so "still ongoing" is unambiguous from "not filled in yet" in both DB and form UI;
  checking it disables/clears end_date.
- No completeness gating before triggering generation - single-user tool, profile will be filled
  in thoroughly before first use; not worth designing a "what counts as complete" rule.
- Dashboard form: one single scrollable page, all sections stacked (personal info -> skills ->
  experience -> education -> projects), singleton record auto-available (no explicit "create
  profile" step), per-row CRUD for each list.
- Form validates end_date >= start_date and blocks save on violation; end_date required unless
  is_current is checked.

Grilled and confirmed with user: 3 rounds, 16 questions total.
notes: Amended by applyr-n58.6 (CV template design): added photo_path (nullable) and show_photo (boolean) fields to MasterProfile personal info, to support an optional CV header photo. Schema table above is otherwise unchanged.
close_reason: MasterProfile schema grilled and confirmed with user (3 rounds, 16 questions). Full schema (personal info, Experience/Education/Project child tables, skills JSON, dashboard form design) recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md MasterProfile definition sharpened to include personal/contact info and the fact/reframe rule.

title: Design SearchProfile schema
description:
## Question

What fields make up a SearchProfile (the saved set of search parameters matched against job boards)? The user named keyword, lokasi (location), min pengalaman (minimum experience), and rentang tanggal post (post-date range) as the starting set — grill to confirm exact shape/types for each, whether a user can have multiple SearchProfiles active at once (implied yes, per the map's "one Application per Job regardless of how many SearchProfiles matched it" decision), how a SearchProfile maps onto each platform's own search/filter parameters (Glints and JobStreet may not expose identical filters), and any other fields needed (e.g. job type, remote/onsite, salary floor) that weren't in the original list.
design:
## SearchProfile schema (v1)

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| name | string, required | User-facing label; needed since multiple profiles can be active at once |
| is_active | boolean | Paused profiles skipped by poller, history retained |
| keyword | string[] | OR-matched terms |
| location | string | Free text (e.g. "Jakarta Selatan"); resolved to each platform's own location IDs at adapter level |
| country_code | string, unconstrained | Dynamic/no enum; only "ID" functionally supported until a non-Indonesia adapter variant exists (JobStreet is domain-per-country, not param-per-country) |
| min_experience_years | integer, nullable | |
| max_experience_years | integer, nullable | |
| post_date_range | enum: PAST_24_HOURS \| PAST_WEEK \| PAST_MONTH \| ANY_TIME | Matches Glints' actual bucketed capability, not an arbitrary date range |
| work_arrangement | enum: remote \| onsite \| hybrid \| any | |
| job_type | enum: full_time \| part_time \| contract \| internship \| any | |

## Decisions
- Multiple active SearchProfiles per user, run independently.
- Canonical schema + per-Adapter best-effort translation to native query params (see CONTEXT.md SearchProfile entry).
- Salary floor excluded from v1 (deferred as post-fetch display/sort concern, not a search filter).
- No operational/run-state fields on SearchProfile (last-run timestamp, dedup cursor belongs to n58.7's polling/scheduling design, not this schema).
- Reference facts pulled from applyr-n58.1 findings: Glints searchJobsV3 input fields (SearchTerm, CountryCode, HierarchicalLocationId*/CityId, lastUpdatedAtRange enum, min/maxYearsOfExperience, isRemote, workArrangementOptions); JobStreet jobSearchV7 exact keyword/location/date-range placement still unresolved (adapter-build mechanical follow-up, not a schema blocker).
close_reason: SearchProfile schema grilled and confirmed with user (9 questions, 2 rounds). Full field table recorded in issue design field; CONTEXT.md SearchProfile definition sharpened to match.

title: Investigate Glints & JobStreet internal JSON APIs
description:
## Question

Do Glints and JobStreet expose an internal JSON API (reachable without auth, without triggering anti-bot blocking) that a job-search Adapter could call directly, or does the Adapter need to fall back to HTML-selector parsing / Browsershot headless browsing for one or both platforms?

Investigate Glints first, then JobStreet, in the same session. For each platform: search a role with typical params (keyword, location, date range) in a real browser, inspect network requests for JSON XHR/fetch calls that return job listing data, and try calling that endpoint directly (no browser) to see if it responds normally or gets blocked/challenged. Note any auth/session/cookie requirements, rate-limit signals, and response shape (what fields are present).

This is a high-risk prototype ticket per the map's Destination: it validates external facts (not a design preference) that the Job canonical-model ticket and the monitoring/alerting ticket both depend on.
notes:
## Findings

### Glints — API confirmed usable directly, no fallback needed

- Search page (`glints.com/id/opportunities/jobs/explore`) is a Next.js app, loads fine unauthenticated, SSRs initial results into an Apollo-cache blob (`__NEXT_DATA__`).
- GraphQL endpoint: `POST https://glints.com/api/v2/graphql` (candidate-facing client; `/api/graphql` and `/api/v2-alc/graphql` also exist for other client variants).
- No auth needed — response body includes `"isAuthenticated": false` when called with zero cookies.
- Anti-bot: Cloudflare fronts it. A generic bare `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0` gets hard-blocked (`403`, `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`, Cloudflare "Firewall" interstitial). A realistic full desktop Chrome UA string alone — no cookies, no Referer — was enough to pass. Bot-scoring here appears to key mainly off UA plausibility, not a JS/Turnstile challenge.
- No rate-limiting observed across 15 rapid sequential requests.
- Schema introspection is **enabled** in production — queried the live schema directly.
- Confirmed working query: `searchJobsV3(data: JobSearchConditionInput): JobSearchResults`.
  - Relevant input fields: `SearchTerm` (keyword list), `CountryCode`, `HierarchicalLocationIdLevel1-4`/`CityId` (location), `lastUpdatedAtRange` (enum: `PAST_24_HOURS`/`PAST_WEEK`/`PAST_MONTH`/`ANY_TIME` — **bucketed, not an arbitrary date range**), `minYearsOfExperience`/`maxYearsOfExperience`, `isRemote`, `workArrangementOptions`, `page`/`pageSize`/`offset`/`limit`, `sortBy`, `sources`.
  - Result shape: `totalJobs`, `hasMore`, `jobsInPage: [Job]`.
  - `Job` fields available: id, title, company{id,name}, city/citySubDivision/country/location, createdAt/updatedAt/startDate/endDate/expiryDate, min/maxYearsOfExperience, isRemote, workArrangementOption, salaries/salaryEstimate, skills, benefits, descriptionJsonString, externalApplyURL, status, type, source, educationLevel, gender, labels.
  - Ran a live end-to-end query for "software engineer" / Indonesia / PAST_WEEK and got real current postings back.
- **Verdict: use the JSON API directly. No HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot needed for Glints job search.**

### JobStreet — API confirmed reachable, exact request shape not fully pinned down

- Domain: `jobstreet.co.id` now 308-redirects to `id.jobstreet.com` (SEEK's consolidated domain, same backend platform as SEEK AU/NZ and JobsDB). **Adapter should target `id.jobstreet.com`.**
- GraphQL endpoint: same-origin proxy at `https://id.jobstreet.com/graphql` (backs onto `candidate-graphql(-dark)-prod.cloud.seek.com.au`).
- Anti-bot: Cloudflare fronts it, and it's more header-sensitive than Glints — a request missing standard browser headers (`Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `sec-ch-ua*`) on the plain HTML search page itself gets hard-blocked (`403`, `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`, Turnstile CSP present). Adding a full realistic header set (proper `Accept`/`Accept-Language`/`sec-ch-ua*` plus a real UA) got a normal `200` with real SSR job data embedded (`totalCount` present) — no JS challenge actually had to be solved in this test.
- With that same header set, POSTing directly to `/graphql` (no cookies, no auth) reaches the real Apollo Server and returns real GraphQL validation errors, not a block. No blocking/rate-limiting observed across 10 rapid identical requests.
- Introspection is **disabled** in production (Apollo Server hardening) — had to recover the schema from the frontend's minified JS bundles instead.
- Found the real operation used by the search results page: `jobSearchV7(params: JobSearchV7QueryInput!)`, called alongside `$locale`/`$zone`/`$country`/`$timezone`/`$tagsSubType`. Extracted the full ~300-line field selection the live frontend actually requests, which includes: id, title, abstract, advertiser/organisation, categories, location (incl. seoHierarchy), work types/work arrangements, salary (min/max/currency/period + display value), listedAt (posted date), tags, url, and activity/analytics counts (impressions, application starts/ends) — richer than Glints in some respects (salary display formatting, activity stats).
  - Live validation-error probing (GraphQL errors are precise about missing/unknown fields) confirmed `params` requires only `searchContext: JobSearchV7SearchContextInput!` and `sessionId: String!` at the top level; `searchContext` in turn requires `brand`/`intent`/`source` enums (plausible values recovered from the bundle: brand `"jobstreet"`, intent `"SEARCH"`, source `"FE_REVERSAL"`; not yet confirmed which combination is canonical for a fresh keyword search).
  - **Open item**: exactly where keyword / location / date-range / pagination land in the input shape wasn't resolved this session — they're not direct children of `params` or `searchContext` as tried. The frontend maps URL query params into these GraphQL variables via a client-side step this investigation didn't fully trace. This is a mechanical follow-up (e.g. capture one real outgoing request from an actual browser devtools session) for whoever builds the JobStreet adapter — not a feasibility blocker.
  - `sessionId` is a client-generated value (from Redux state), not a server-issued auth/session cookie — a request-shape requirement, not an auth requirement.
- **Verdict: the JSON API is real and reachable directly, unauthenticated, without anti-bot blocking, given realistic browser headers.** Finishing the exact `JobSearchV7QueryInput` shape is adapter-implementation detail, not a reason to fall back to HTML/Browsershot.

### Answer to the ticket's question

Neither platform needs to fall back to HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot headless browsing for job search. Both expose internal GraphQL JSON APIs reachable directly over plain HTTP, unauthenticated, provided requests carry realistic browser-like headers (User-Agent alone sufficed for Glints; a fuller standard header set was needed for JobStreet). Cloudflare fronts both, but in this session its bot-scoring was satisfied by header realism alone — no JS challenge had to be solved, no login/cookies/session required. No rate-limiting surfaced in short bursts (10-15 rapid sequential requests) on either platform; that doesn't rule out slower-forming, volume-based throttling, so the real adapter should still pace requests and back off on 403/429 — and the monitoring/alerting ticket (n58.7) should treat a Cloudflare challenge response (`403` + `Cf-Mitigated: challenge` header) as the concrete signal to alert on.

### Notes for downstream tickets

- **Job canonical model (n58.5)**: use the union of Glints' `Job` fields and JobStreet's `JobSearchV7` job fields above as the field-shape reference.
- **Adapter monitoring/alerting (n58.7)**: alert on Cloudflare challenge responses (`403` + `Cf-Mitigated: challenge`) — that's the observed anti-bot escalation signature for both platforms.
- **JobStreet domain**: target `id.jobstreet.com`, not `jobstreet.co.id` (which redirects).
close_reason: Both platforms confirmed to expose directly-callable, unauthenticated internal GraphQL JSON APIs (Glints: /api/v2/graphql searchJobsV3, introspection enabled; JobStreet: id.jobstreet.com/graphql jobSearchV7, introspection disabled, schema reverse-engineered from JS bundles). No fallback to HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot needed for job search on either platform. Cloudflare bot-mitigation on both was satisfied by realistic browser headers alone in this session; JobStreet's exact query-variable shape needs a small mechanical follow-up when the adapter is actually built. Full findings in issue notes.

title: Applyr Wayfinder Map
description:
## Destination

A complete technical spec — SearchProfile schema, canonical Job model, MasterProfile schema (with its dashboard-form design), Application status-tracking design, a single generic CV/cover-letter HTML template design, and an adapter monitoring/alerting strategy — for an automated job-application assistant covering **Glints and JobStreet only**. Ready to hand off for implementation. This map is planning-only, except prototype tickets that validate high-risk external facts before architecture is locked in.

## Notes

- Domain vocabulary is locked in `CONTEXT.md` at repo root (SearchProfile, Adapter, Job, MasterProfile, TailoredApplication, Application). Consult it before any ticket that touches these terms; challenge and update it if a ticket's answer sharpens or conflicts with a definition.
- Fixed architectural decisions — do NOT re-grill these, they came pre-settled from the user:
  - Scraping: adapter pattern per platform (fetch/parse/normalize); check for an internal JSON API before falling back to HTML parsing (selector or Browsershot headless).
  - Dedup by platform+external_id, checked BEFORE a Job enters AI tailoring.
  - AI tailoring: Gemini API Flash (free tier). Hard constraint: title/company/period must match MasterProfile exactly; AI may only reframe description/achievements.
  - AI output must be structured JSON via Gemini's responseSchema, never freeform-parsed text.
  - Programmatic fact validation before render; a failed validation triggers regeneration (discard the failed attempt, don't keep it).
  - Rate limiting for Gemini free tier (~8 req/min via queue rate limiter). 429s use exponential backoff; validation-failure retries use regenerate logic — these two retry paths stay separate, never merged.
  - Render pipeline: validated JSON → Blade HTML template → PDF via Browsershot.
  - Notifications: Telegram bot + dashboard web (not WhatsApp). Dashboard is also where the user reviews/edits before applying and tracks application status.
  - AI provider abstracted behind one interface, so swapping providers later doesn't require touching the pipeline.
  - Stack: Laravel (queue jobs, Blade templating).
- Skills to consult per ticket: grilling + domain-modeling for schema/design tickets; the "prototype" skill for the platform-API validation ticket.
- CV/cover-letter template: one generic template for v1 — no per-role variants (see Out of scope).
- Adapter monitoring/alerting reuses the Telegram bot channel; alert after consecutive failures, not on the first failure.
- MasterProfile is authored/edited via a dashboard form, not a config file.
- Platform investigation order: Glints before JobStreet.

## Decisions so far

- **applyr-n58.1 (closed)**: Both Glints and JobStreet expose directly-callable, unauthenticated internal GraphQL JSON APIs for job search — no HTML-selector parsing or Browsershot fallback needed for either platform. Glints: `POST glints.com/api/v2/graphql`, `searchJobsV3`, introspection enabled. JobStreet: `POST id.jobstreet.com/graphql` (not jobstreet.co.id, which redirects), `jobSearchV7`, introspection disabled, schema recovered from frontend JS. Both sit behind Cloudflare bot-mitigation that was satisfied by realistic browser headers alone (no JS challenge solved, no auth/cookies needed). Full field-shape findings captured on the issue for n58.5 (canonical Job model) to consume; Cloudflare-challenge response signature captured for n58.7 (monitoring/alerting) to alert on.
- **applyr-n58.6 (closed)**: Single generic CV/cover-letter template design locked. Two separate PDFs per TailoredApplication (`cv.pdf`, `cover_letter.pdf`), minimalist single-column Inter (self-hosted) layout with section-separator rules. TailoredApplication's `cv_data`/`cover_letter_data` JSON are full self-contained snapshots (copied facts + reframed content, keyed by MasterProfile entry id) — the Gemini `responseSchema` itself stays narrow (only description/achievements per entry, only the three cover-letter paragraph fields), since skills and the cover letter's greeting/date/subject/sign-off are deterministic facts assembled by the app, never sent to the AI. Achievements may be curated down when reframed but never invented beyond MasterProfile's list. Amends MasterProfile (n58.3) with an optional photo (`photo_path` + `show_photo` toggle), rendered top-left in the CV header only.

## Not yet specified

- Dashboard deployment/hosting details beyond "single-user, no-auth" — not yet explored.
- Implementation order/build roadmap beyond this spec map (this map produces a spec, not a build schedule).

## Out of scope

- LinkedIn adapter — ToS/anti-bot risk is a different class than Glints/JobStreet; a separate effort if pursued later.
- Multi-user/auth dashboard — this is a personal tool, not a multi-tenant product.
- Per-role CV/cover-letter template variants (e.g. SA vs QA) — v1 destination is one generic template; variants are ruled out of this map's scope, not merely deferred.
